title: Biological reading of the two-type model in one macrophage-associated compartment
status: alternate — not currently included in main.tex; see NOTE_alternate.md
tool: TikZ/PGF via pdflatex (TeX Live 2024); Ghostscript 10.05 for PNG; dvisvgm 3.2.2 + libgs for SVG
biology_source: flow_D.pdf — Biphasic Pathogenesis of Yersinia pestis (YCV, F1/Psa/T3SS package)
intended_placement: Immediately after Table tab:bio-mapping in sec:biology / 5.1, at width=\textwidth
palette_note: Rate symbols and event arrows use the canonical manuscript accents (identical to fig01/fig05). Drawn bacterial bodies use lowered-chroma tints of the same two hues; type 1 is deliberately lighter than type 2 so the two states separate in greyscale as well as in hue.

accessibility.colour_blind: Okabe-Ito blue/vermillion pair; deuteranope- and protanope-safe
accessibility.greyscale: checked with gs -sDEVICE=pnggray; type 1 (light) vs type 2 (dark + halo + surface hairs) remain distinct, and the conversion ramp is still legible via the three transitional rods
accessibility.printed_size: checked at 6.5 in text width; all of X_t, Y_t, lambda_i, mu_i, nu, delta_i, tau_c legible

scientific_caveats: Type 2 is a coarse-grained latent adapted state, not a claim that every bacterium has completed a molecular programme
delta_i are effective per-capita associations with containment failure, not proof of active rupture by either type
delta_1 and delta_2 arrows are drawn with identical weight and both reach the same endpoint, so no regime (EQ / MAT / GATE / EARLY) is privileged
The type-2 surface cue (halo plus sparse hairlines) is schematic and is not labelled as a demonstrated trigger of release; the T3SS is not depicted as the intracellular survival engine
The break in the host-cell boundary is restrained; no exploding-cell imagery
Extracellular aftermath is drawn at reduced opacity and labelled as outside the model
design_departures_from_brief: Two vacuolar outlines rather than one, to keep the left-to-right sequence readable; the right-hand one is labelled 'same compartment' so no second compartment type is implied
The conversion band uses 48 discrete colour strips rather than a true gradient, so the PDF and SVG outputs are identical (PostScript shadings do not survive the DVI->SVG route)
Bacterial bodies use muted tints while rate symbols keep the canonical accents, preserving continuity with fig01 without making the biology look like a state diagram
